routineClass.statement: **The `routine` review class is justified on this head.** Every edit is a type annotation (or the `as const` that task 1.2 names); the emitted JavaScript of the whole root project is byte-identical between base and head under the repo compiler, re-derived here with my own scripts and matched hash-for-hash against the author's receipt; the two campaign-grant files and the auth/identity crypto code emit identical bytes; and the one exported-signature change (the `BufferSource` widening) cannot change any runtime path (section 2). tasks02Measurement.result: Task 0.2 scratch measurement on the TS7S1A pre-edit baseline 4bf26f7b with the D2 config edits in an uncommitted scratch copy. TypeScript 7.0.2 root: 11 errors, exactly the design.md Context list (BranchCheckpointCache.ts 352, 377 TS2322; auth.ts 215, 223; IdentityService.ts 159, 165, 182, 188, 330, 355, 384). TypeScript 6.0.3 root: 9, the BufferSource ones only. Desktop tsconfig.json and tsconfig.test.json: 0 on both. TS2769/TS2345 report only the first bad argument of a call, and three more errors were hidden behind them, all in IdentityService.ts: the verifySignature verify data argument at line 188, the encryptWithPassword encrypt data argument at 357 and the decryptWithPassword decrypt ciphertext argument at 386. That makes 12 BufferSource sites on both compilers. After the TS7S1A edits, TypeScript 7.0.2 and 6.0.3 report 0/0/0 for root, desktop/tsconfig.json and desktop/tsconfig.test.json, and npm run typecheck (5.8.3) reports 0.

tasks02Measurement.reviewerHiddenErrors: Hidden first-bad-argument errors (`followon-probe.cjs`, my own: TS 5.8 parser locates the identifier at each reported position, rewrites a call argument to `(x as any)` or a shorthand property to `x: (x as any)`, re-runs, repeats; `git checkout -- src` afterwards, status back to the two D2 files): round 1 neutralises the 9, round 2 exposes **3 more** (`IdentityService.ts` `verify(... data)` on line 188, `encrypt(... data)` 357, `decrypt(... ciphertext)` 386), round 3 leaves only the two TS2322 under TS7 and nothing under TS6. **12 distinct `BufferSource` sites under both 7.0.2 and 6.0.3**, matching the author and the tasks.md outcome line. Position note: the second-round `data` on line 188 is reported at column 73 only because the first-round wrap lengthened the line; in the pristine base text it sits at (188,63). The author's receipts quote 73 (minor N1).
tasks02Measurement.reviewerDesignMd: **Does design.md's "9 x TS2769/TS2345" need a follow-up edit?** Not as a correction: the sentence describes what TypeScript 7 *reports*, and it still reports exactly 9 + 2 on the unmodified base. The registration receipt's `designMdNineErrors` treats the count as superseded by the unit text and routes design.md to TS7S1B's 0.2 conditional leaf, which fires only if the list changed; it did not. The tasks.md 1.1 outcome line now carries the real count (12 arguments) in the file an implementer reads first, which satisfies the unit's MUST. A one-sentence clarification in design.md is optional and belongs to TS7S1B if the owner wants design.md self-contained (carry-forward C1 gives the wording); nothing on this head is wrong.

laterUnits.admissionWarningsIntro: Additions I would make to the admission warnings for any future `routine`-by-byte-identical-emit unit:

admissionWarnings.wording: The admission receipt must name the emit-proof roots (whole project vs changed-file roots) and the option sets, and the independent reviewer must reproduce the per-file output hashes, not only the PASS verdict.
Quote compiler error positions from the pristine baseline text; label any position measured after an in-place neutralisation as such.

The sensitivity set must include at least one mutation inside the security-relevant leaf's control flow and one type-only change that must not be flagged, run through the same script that produced the equality verdict.
